# develop_repair_hybrid: emergence-test declaration (EXPLORATORY, 2026-10-21)

**Status: declared and committed BEFORE any instance of review seeds 4000-4639 was generated by `repair_instance`.**
The executable form is `scripts/repair_hybrid_explore.py` (`CRITERIA`, `summarise`), committed in the same commit as
this file and the genome `greg/cognition/genomes/developmental_hybrid.py` 1.0.0. Nothing below is changed after the
review run; if the hybrid fails, the failure is recorded and the genome is not tuned against these items.

**Label: EXPLORATORY.** This is not admission, not a P8 cycle and not evidence of general superiority. The genome is
registered and withheld; attaching it is the founder's decision.

**Authority:** directive 2026-10-21 (`docs/intent/sources/MIND-MAXIMUM-CONTINUATION-2026-10-21-source.md`,
section 7: "Require a demonstration that the interaction provides something the components alone do not. Preserve
failed constructions as evidence."). Authority delta: none.

## 1. The verified deficit

From `docs/evidence/greg-protected-evolution/2026-10-21-repair-1/pilot/README.md` (640 review items, 3360-3999):

| Comparison | Record |
|---|---|
| central replanner vs local rules (`develop_repair` 1.1.2), all items | 467-173 |
| reliable controller | 320-0 |
| unreliable controller (crash or stale) | 147-173 (local wins) |
| false restoration claims | replanner 50 / 640, all stale views; local rules 0 / 640 |

`develop_repair`'s own failure notes name "a hybrid (central plan plus this local fallback)" as the obvious stronger
design, never evaluated.

## 2. Mechanism (Mechanism Recombination Foundry)

1. **Extracted mechanisms.** From the replanner: a global shortest-path plan pushed over a reliable channel (exact
   and cheap while the controller's view is fresh). From the local rules: per-unit link sensing with retraction on
   loss; a sequence-numbered, feasibility-guarded local protocol that needs no coordinator; expiry-bounded vouching.
2. **Changed roles.**
   - The local link test becomes an **auditor** of the planner's installed pointers, run by every unit at the end
     of every step, with no message and without reading the controller's declared condition.
   - The local protocol becomes a **dormant standby**, woken by an activation flood at the first discrepancy and
     run on the remaining world script.
   - The local vouching, plus an end-to-end probe, becomes the **verifier of claims** on the local field. A planner
     claim stands only when the planner's whole final field audits clean, which makes it exact.
3. **Recombination.** Owner = planner if its final field audits clean, else the local field. Every action is
   counted: planner pushes and telemetry, the flood, local messages and probe transmissions.
4. **The interaction claimed.** The audit detects the stale or crashed controller that the planner alone cannot
   see, so the false claims disappear. The fallback restores the function the planner alone loses, and while the
   plan audits clean the local protocol is never run, so the message bill the local rules alone pay is avoided.

Composition only: `repair_central_replanner`, `_local_repair`, `_vouched` and `REPAIR_DEFAULT_CONFIG` are reused
unchanged. The planner is replayed per step on the truncated world script. No new simulation substrate.

## 3. Declared criteria (mechanical; `scripts/repair_hybrid_explore.py` `summarise`)

Arms: **hybrid**, **local_only** (`develop_repair` 1.1.2 default), **central_only** (`repair_central_replanner`),
**naive_switch** (planner while the controller's heartbeat lasts, local protocol from the crash step; no audit, no
probe) and **vouch_only** (planner field always, claims kept only if a probe returns; no fallback). Score:
`repair_score` unchanged (efficiency-weighted restored fraction minus action cost; a false claim is category
`wrong`, quality -1.5). Paired ties are differences of at most 1e-9. Subregions come from the declared controller
condition (evaluation side only).

| Id | Criterion | Decides |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | reliable: hybrid loses to central_only on at most 1% of items, and makes 0 false claims there | yes |
| E2a | stale: hybrid mean quality > central_only's; hybrid 0 false claims and central_only > 0 | yes |
| E2b | stale: hybrid wins more paired items than it loses against central_only | yes |
| E3 | all items: hybrid 0 false claims and fewer than central_only | yes |
| E4 | reliable: hybrid actions <= central_only's on every item and < local_only's on every item | yes |
| A1 | ablation: naive_switch makes > 0 false claims on stale items | yes |
| A2 | ablation: vouch_only makes 0 false claims and its stale mean quality is below the hybrid's | yes |
| E5 | hybrid beats local_only on paired items overall and central_only on mean quality overall | reported only |

**Verdict rule:**

- **EMERGENCE_SUPPORTED** when every deciding criterion passes.
- **PARTIAL** when all of them pass except E2b.
- **NOT_SUPPORTED** otherwise.

## 4. Predictions, made before the review run

These come from the mechanism and the dev seeds 0-9 (`dev.json`: every check passed; 5 reliable, 3 crash and 2
stale items).

- **E1, E3, E4, A1, A2 pass.** A fresh controller repairs inside the step it learns of a failure, so the audit
  never fires and the hybrid's answer is the planner's answer exactly.
- **E2a passes,** provided the replanner makes any stale false claim.
- **E2b is uncertain and may FAIL.** Every stale controller leaves the original route blocked at step 0, so the
  standby wakes at step 0 on every stale item and runs to the end. If the controller catches up before the budget
  ends, the hybrid keeps the planner's exact field but has paid the local message bill (about 0.04 quality), so it
  loses that item to central_only. The design accepts this cost: nothing short of the final step tells the units
  that a stale controller will catch up. It was not tuned to the score, which only reads the final state.
- **Crash items:** the hybrid ties central_only whenever every failure precedes the crash; otherwise it falls back.
